articles.title: Football connects communities but can pull them apart if governed carelessly
articles.summary: Sport is a space to help youngsters develop character, resilience and confidence, but we need stronger leadership and safer environments to make this happen. The fight for the soul of football isn’t just happening in the offices of Uefa and Fifa, it’s taking place on pitches much closer to home.
body: This isn’t just a Scottish problem. Contacts I speak to in different roles around football confirm and almost accept that “youth football is atrocious”. This should be sounding major alarm bells, for the consequences go way beyond the pitch. The existing disciplinary systems and PR campaigns are not nearly enough to address and change the situation.

There is no shortage of evidence about how important it is – whether you are trying to develop skilful football players or healthy young people – that children need space to play, try stuff out and thrive. We also know that it’s what children want from sport. Research by Amanda Visek at the Milken Institute of Public Health at George Washington University, confirms that when it comes to organised sport, kids just want to have fun. What counts for girls and boys are things like trying your best, working hard, playing well together as a team. When mapping 81 determinants of fun, “winning” ranked 40th in importance.

The Campaign for Children’s Rights in Football is an independent and impartial organisation. It’s preparing to launch and trying to create a greater platform for its work in the sport internationally. It’s needed more than ever.
points: Sport is a space to help youngsters develop character, resilience and confidence, but we need stronger leadership and safer environments to make this happen.
The fight for the soul of football isn’t just happening in the offices of Uefa and Fifa, it’s taking place on pitches much closer to home.

articles.title: Tiger Woods set for plea change in Florida DUI case after rollover crash
articles.summary: Woods plans to change not guilty plea in DUI case. Change-of-plea hearing set for 8.30am Wednesday. Charges stem from March rollover crash in Florida. Tiger Woods plans to change his not guilty plea in the DUI case stemming from a rollover crash near his Florida home earlier this year, according to…
body: The 50-year-old golf star is due to appear in Martin County circuit court at 8.30am on Wednesday for a change-of-plea hearing before judge Darren Steele. Woods had previously pleaded not guilty to charges of driving under the influence with property damage and refusing to submit to a lawful test.
The filing did not disclose what plea Woods intends to enter or provide further details about the expected change.

The charges stem from a 27 March crash in Hobe Sound, near Woods’s residence on Jupiter Island. Martin County sheriff John Budensiek said Woods was driving a Land Rover that overturned after he attempted to overtake a truck on a narrow two-lane road shortly before 2pm.

The truck had been slowing to turn into a driveway when Woods approached at what Budensiek described as a “high rate of speed” on a road with a 30mph limit. Woods’s vehicle clipped a trailer, veered off and came to rest on its driver’s side after sliding along the roadway.

articles.title: Are Arsenal taking a risk in not signing a world-class forward?
articles.summary: Arsenal have been busy in the transfer market as they look to defend their Premier League title, but do they lack a world class striker still?
body: That was manager Mikel Arteta's aim for Arsenal 's transfer dealings following their defeat by Paris St-Germain in the Champions League final in May.

The Gunners won their first title in 22 years last season by seven points and did not lose a game in the Champions League during normal time, with their only loss in the competition coming to Luis Enrique's side on penalties.
But it was clear coming into the summer transfer window that the club were looking for a game-changing attacker to lift their forward line.

Viktor Gyokeres - a £64m signing last summer from Portuguese side Sporting - scored 21 goals in his first season for Arsenal but his performances still raised questions about whether he is the best fit for Arteta's side going forward.

articles.title: In-form Coco Gauff serves notice with assured start to US Open title pursuit
articles.summary: Gauff tops Sonmez 6-3, 6-4 in first-round match. American saves three break points in pivotal hold. Fourth seed also has world No 1 ranking in sight. Coco Gauff returned to the scene of her grand slam breakthrough on a rain-lashed Tuesday night and safely cleared the first hurdle toward another…
body: The 22-year-old American, seeded fourth in New York, arrived with momentum and expectation running unusually high, fresh off her first title of the year in Cincinnati and having shown encouraging signs that the serve which has so often dictated the rest of her game is becoming a more reliable weapon. Now, three years after she first lifted the trophy here, both a third major championship and the world No 1 ranking are within her reach.

Gauff got off to a confident start before a buzzing crowd, crunching a pair of early aces in a love hold, but the 54th-ranked Sonmez held her own in the muscular baseline exchanges throughout the opening five games. Gauff took control in the sixth, breaking her opponent’s serve without dropping a point, then steadied herself through an uneven service game to move to the brink of the set at 5-2. Sonmez held to prolong it, but Gauff calmly served it out after 33 minutes as the heavy rainfall pounding the roof overhead reverberated through Ashe like the inside of a bass drum.

body: Only a handful of games into the Scottish Premiership season and it could be argued that about half its team managers are already looking nervously over their shoulders.

At least most do not have to deal with a transfer deadline day before preparing for this midweek's fixtures as the domestic deadline has been delayed until the dust had settled on the five games scheduled for Wednesday evening.

However, while they have another chance to assess their reshaped squads before another hasty round of phone calls and negotiations before the transfer window closes at 17:00 BST on Thursday, Heart of Midlothian and Hibernian have no such luxury as they meet later that evening.
So what should we look out for in that big game - and the five others on Wednesday?

articles.title: Everton left with only one striker after Balogun deal collapses late on deadline day
articles.summary: 25-year-old walks away from £40m deal at last moment. Beto and Ndiaye already sold by club to raise funds. Everton’s £40m move for US international Folarin Balogun collapsed late on deadline day to leave manager David Moyes with only one striker for the first half of the season.
body: Everton had agreed a £40m deal for Balogun only for issues with the striker’s medical to place the transfer in doubt after the Merseyside club had sold Beto to Fiorentina and Iliman Ndiaye to Manchester City. Enquiries were made to Manchester United for Joshua Zirkzee and Aston Villa for Tammy Abraham but proposed loans for both forwards were rejected.

The structure of the deal was renegotiated late on – Monaco agreed to accept a lower payment up front and more in add-ons – and Everton submitted a deal sheet to complete the transfer in time. But the 25-year-old is said to have changed his mind over the move and walked away at the final moment. The collapse of the deal leaves Thierno Barry as Everton’s one recognised striker and completed a shambolic end to the window by the club’s hierarchy, who were already under pressure having tried to sell Harrison Armstrong to Nottingham Forest.

articles.title: Paredes puts question mark over Argentina future
articles.summary: Argentina midfielder Leandro Paredes says it is going to be "difficult" for him to continue playing for his country in the wake of his 10-match international ban.
body: Paredes received the suspension from Fifa for his part in an on-pitch confrontation following Argentina's 1-0 defeat by Spain in the 2026 World Cup final.
The 32-year-old grabbed Spain's Eric Garcia by the throat and wrestled Gavi to the ground, before appearing to strike the latter in the face.
Paredes also suggested Argentina legend Lionel Messi retiring from international football could play a part in his decision.
"It's going to be difficult for me to stay with the national team," said Boca Juniors player Paredes.

articles.title: From Sam’s Club to Saturdays | Kohen Maroney’s unlikely journey back to football
articles.summary: Kohen Maroney taught himself to kick on a Lubbock middle school field before returning home to Wichita Falls an All-LSC kicker at Midwestern State.
body: Nearly two years ago, Kohen Maroney began showing up at a middle school field in Lubbock, Texas, to do a job no one had hired him for.
No coach was waiting for him, and no roster spot was guaranteed. Maroney, a freshman at Texas Tech and working at Sam’s Club, was trying to figure out how to get football back into his life.
“I was just a regular student, and I worked at Sam’s Club,” Maroney said. “In my free time, I would go to that little middle school field, like I said, six days a week.”

Maroney graduated from the former Rider High School (now Rider Middle School) in 2024 after playing wide receiver and strong safety. He kicked some in high school, mostly on pooch kickoffs, but had never treated it as a position he could seriously pursue.

body: Kimi Antonelli leads his Mercedes team-mate George Russell and Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton by 59 points at the top of the standings, with McLaren's Lando Norris 83 points back in fourth after belatedly igniting his title defence with victories at the last two races.

Given the significant margins by which the British duo each trail Antonelli, it has been a topic of speculation as to whether either Ferrari or McLaren would consider implementing team orders sooner rather than later to aid their better-positioned driver in the title fight.

articles.title: AEW show in Athens marks former Bulldog Wix Patton's return | Exclusive
articles.summary: Former Georgia Bulldog Wix Patton has spent much of his adult life reinventing himself. The former University of Georgia tight end left football to pursue a music career, touring nationally as a hip-hop artist and performer. Now, he's embarking on a third act as a professional wrestler.
body: Patton will make his first Athens wrestling appearance on Sept. 9 during AEW's "Rebel Heart Dynamite" live taping at Akins Ford Arena, marking a homecoming for a figure whose athletic and creative careers have deep ties to the city. Doors open at 6:30 p.m., and the event begins at 7:30 p.m.

For fans who have followed Patton's career from football to music, the move might seem unexpected. But Patton sees wrestling as the natural intersection of athletics and entertainment, the two worlds that have shaped him the most.
"I already love performing, and I do it with my music," Patton said. "Being able to go out there and put on a show and really play into the exaggerated character, it's just so fun."

Patton's previous reinvention came in 2020, when he walked away from Georgia's football program to focus on music full-time. At the time, Patton told the Banner-Herald that football and music had been intertwined throughout his life, with lessons learned on the field helping him navigate the recording industry.

articles.title: Balogun walks away from Everton deal
articles.summary: Everton's move for Monaco striker Folarin Balogun has fallen through following a change of heart from the player after the deal scuppered Chelsea's chances of signing Lamine Camara.
body: Balogun arrived in Merseyside at lunchtime to complete the £40m Deadline Day transfer, but doubts began to emerge that the deal would be completed after an issue came up in the medical.
As a result, Monaco moved to sell midfielder Camara instead, but in another twist, Everton renegotiated Balogun's deal to force the move through.
Despite having a full agreement to sell Camara to Chelsea in place, Monaco withdrew from the deal as the 11pm transfer deadline passed, which left the Blues furious.
Chelsea also had the chance to withdraw from the £125m move to sell Enzo Fernandez to Man City, but chose not to out of good faith.
